Hi Tom — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what I heard
- Priority: Fully air-gapped, on-prem deployment inside LegacyBank data centers. No persistent outbound connections.
- Key constraints: procurement lead times, limited maintenance windows, internal KMS/HSM for key material, strict change control for model/infra updates.
- Workloads: low-latency inference for customer-facing workflows (peak qps ~350 across several services).

Open questions we flagged on the call
- Hardware footprint & GPU recommendations for target throughput
- Offline / air-gap upgrade process and signing model updates
- Telemetry / telemetry opt-out and audit logging retention
- OS / distro requirements and support windows

Attachments: I'm sharing our on-prem requirements doc and a hardware checklist to start (see attached). These are our standard starting artifacts — we'll tailor them to your DC specifics after the technical deep dive.

Immediate next steps
1) Please review the attached redwood_onprem_requirements_v1.pdf and hardware-checklist.xlsx and flag anything that won't work for your environment (target: EOD Wed 6/24).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive: engineering + infra (I propose Tue 6/23 10:00am PT). Jonas (cc'd) will join to answer detailed ops/upgrade questions.
3) If procurement wants an initial SOW/ballpark lead time, I can share a draft once we confirm hardware profile.

A few quick answers from our side to unblock you:
- Control plane: can be customer-managed (private control plane) or fully offline. For fully offline we ship a private package and an on-prem console; no telemetry is required.
- Upgrades: we support signed artifacts for model/runtime updates; these can be delivered via USB/air-gapped transfer and validated against a local HSM.
- KMS: we integrate with customer HSM/KMS (PKCS11-compatible).

I'll follow up with Jonas to get the hardware baseline. Thanks — talk soon.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive

2) Offline upgrades: you said signed artifacts via USB — does Redwood provide tooling to verify/sign, or do we need to maintain signing keys in our HSM? How do you handle rollback/recovery if an upgrade fails?

Also: procurement asked for a rough lead time for the on-prem package and any hardware procurement guidance. Can you provide an ETA (weeks) we can include in the RFQ?

If it's useful I can loop in procurement@legacybank.com and our infra lead; let me know who should join the deep-dive.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Hi Tom — great questions. Answering inline and adding a few implementation notes: 

1) GPU guidance
- Ballpark: for ~350 peak qps of low-latency generative inference we typically recommend either: 
  a) 8 x NVIDIA A100 80GB (mixed precision, FP16) for a conservative, well-understood baseline; or
  b) 4–8 x H100 80GB (if you can procure H100s, fewer nodes may be required but plan for driver/CUDA compatibility).
- We'll validate exact counts during the deep-dive using your query length distribution and concurrency targets.

2) Offline upgrades & signing
- We provide tooling to produce signed runtime and model artifacts. Standard flow: Redwood build -> sign -> deliver signed artifact. For air-gapped installs we can support either: 
  a) Redwood provides signed artifacts that you verify in your HSM (preferred for strict control), or
  b) We provide the signing tooling and you run builds internally (we can support an audit trail).
- Rollback: upgrades are transactional with a rollback path; the on-prem orchestrator keeps the previous runtime snapshot locally for immediate revert. We require a maintenance window for schema-changing updates, but minor model patches can be staged without downtime. Details in attached onprem-upgrade-procedures.docx.

3) Telemetry / zero-call-home
- Yes: we support fully offline installs with zero external telemetry. Alternatively, you can enable a heartbeat to an internal endpoint (customer-managed) that only reports health status (no payloads or logs). Audit logs are always stored locally and can be exported on request.

4) OS & images
- We currently certify RHEL 8.6 and Ubuntu 22.04 for our on-prem runtime. We have customers running on hardened RHEL images; we typically onboard by validating kernel modules and container runtime compatibility. If you want to stick with your RHEL baseline, we can do an initial compatibility check during the deep-dive.

Lead times / procurement
- On-prem package (standard air-gapped installer + admin console): 3–4 weeks after PO/contract signature for standard configurations.
- Hardware lead times depend on SKU. A100s are typically 4–8 weeks; H100s vary (often longer). We recommend starting RFQs based on the A100 baseline while we confirm exact counts.

Next step: Jonas and I can run the deep-dive tech session. Proposed times: Tue 6/23 10:00am PT or Wed 6/24 9:00am PT. Please loop in your infra and procurement; procurement@legacybank.com is fine.

I attached our upgrade procedures doc and the hardware checklist contains the initial rack/PSU/host sizing. 

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
